blocks.text: Buckingham Heights Houses: streets and boundaries

items.t: Buckingham Heights is a detached-house slope east and south-east of Deer Lake in south-central Burnaby. Its core streets, Buckingham Drive and Buckingham Avenue, surround Buckingham Elementary School at 6066 Buckingham Avenue, between Deer Lake Park and Royal Oak Avenue.
Deer Lake and Deer Lake Park lie to the north-west and Upper Deer Lake lies to the south-east. Canada Way runs along the north side and Sperling Avenue runs down the park's east side toward the lake.
The board treats Buckingham Heights as its own sub-area, separate from Deer Lake, Deer Lake Place and Upper Deer Lake.

blocks.text: Buckingham Heights Houses: the housing stock

items.t: Detached houses are effectively the whole stock on the Buckingham slope. Housing is concentrated on Buckingham Drive and Buckingham Avenue around the elementary school, with the older heritage-register houses on the Sperling Avenue edge at the park.

Sperling Avenue fronting Deer Lake Park holds early-1900s houses listed in the City's heritage register. The register includes the Woodward House at 5195 Sperling Avenue, built in 1912, inside the Deer Lake Park Heritage Precinct at the slope's north-east edge.

blocks.text: Buckingham Heights Houses: rules that affect buyers

items.t: The houses-specific caution here is the slope and the park edge: heritage-precinct and park-edge lots carry extra review, so confirm eligibility lot by lot before pricing in added units.
For a Sperling Avenue house, check the heritage register before planning a renovation or rebuild.

blocks.text: Buckingham Heights Houses: local details a buyer would not know

items.t: The Deer Lake boat-launch boardwalk is closed for a full replacement until winter 2027. The City gives a signed detour via Sperling Avenue and Deer Lake Drive, adding about five minutes of walking, and a small section of the nearby picnic area is also closed during the work.
Deer Lake Park is open dawn to dusk year-round, and the City calls it the cultural centre of the city.
Permit, tax and grant business for a Buckingham house is handled there, not at a south Burnaby office.

blocks.text: Buckingham Heights Houses: development and new projects

items.t: Status: boardwalk section by the boat launch closed from September 21, 2026, completion scheduled by winter 2027 (as of November 3, 2026).

blocks.text: Buckingham Heights Houses: costs and taxes

items.t: The home owner grant must be claimed by the property tax July due date to avoid penalty.

There is no SkyTrain station inside Buckingham Heights. Royal Oak Station on the Expo Line, to the south-west, is the nearest station named for this side of Burnaby, and the park itself is reached by turning off Canada Way onto Sperling Avenue.

Canada Way runs along the north side, and Royal Oak Avenue runs along the west side toward Kingsway. Buckingham Drive and Buckingham Avenue serve the slope streets, and Sperling Avenue runs down the park's east side.

blocks.text: Buckingham Heights Houses: risks and due diligence

items.t: Check the heritage register and the Deer Lake Park Heritage Precinct before planning work on a Sperling Avenue or lake-edge house. Listed early-1900s houses, such as the Woodward House at 5195 Sperling Avenue built in 1912, carry heritage review that a standard interior street does not.
The lakeshore at the north-west edge is the wet edge, and parcel-level hazard and Agricultural Land Reserve (ALR) status are checked lot by lot through the Agricultural Land Commission.

faq.q: How many houses are for sale in Buckingham Heights?
faq.a: The Greater Vancouver REALTORS® counted 10 houses listed in Buckingham Heights at the end of October 2026. The number changes daily, so ask Jared for today’s count.

faq.q: Is Buckingham Heights a buyers’ or sellers’ market for houses?
faq.a: Buckingham Heights houses sold at a sales ratio of 10% in October 2026, a buyers’ market on the reports’ scale (under 12% favours buyers, over 20% favours sellers).

faq.q: How many houses sold in Buckingham Heights from June to October 2026?
faq.a: Buckingham Heights accounted for 3 of the 251 houses sold across Burnaby from June to October 2026.

faq.q: Which elementary school is inside Buckingham Heights?
faq.a: Buckingham Elementary is the school inside the sub-area, at 6066 Buckingham Avenue. It is a Kindergarten to Grade 7 school in School District 41 (SD41). Catchments are still address-based, so confirm the exact house address in the SD41 locator before relying on this school in an offer.

Burnaby Central Secondary and Moscrop Secondary are the nearest secondaries named. Burnaby Central is at 6011 Deer Lake Parkway, north of the lake, and Moscrop Secondary is at 4433 Moscrop Street, to the west. Which one serves a given Buckingham address is a locator check, not a neighbourhood assumption.

faq.q: Are there condos or townhomes in Buckingham Heights?
faq.a: No attached stock was identified for this sub-area; it reads as a detached, freehold slope. A buyer who needs a strata home should look at the neighbouring sub-areas instead of waiting for attached listings here. Any new attached project would need a City application source, and none inside the sub-area was confirmed.

faq.q: What happens at Deer Lake Park through the year?
faq.a: Deer Lake Park hosts the City's returning 2026 special events on the lawn beside the lake. The City lists Burnaby Blooms on May 3, Symphony and Opera in the Park on July 18 to 19, and the Burnaby Blues and Roots Festival on August 8, with the Haunted Village at Burnaby Village Museum in late October.
